CLASSROOM GIFT IDEAS FOR STUDENTS

NEW TEACHERS

Before I begin this list of classroom gift ideas, I want to add a disclaimer: it’s completely okay to skip classroom gifts or student birthday gifts altogether. There have been years I’ve done student gifts, some years I’ve skipped, and other years we’ve done experiences instead.

I’ll also add, you don’t need to spend a ton of money to give something to your class. Some of my most inexpensive or free items were a bigger hit than larger purchases and things I took time customizing. Now, having said all of that, let’s get into some gift ideas.

CLASSROOM GIFT IDEA: SCHOOL SUPPLIES

I love giving pencils or stickers as student gifts. Throughout the year, I used to pick up a pack of pencils from the dollar store and save them. Then when a holiday would roll around I put them all in a container and let students pick one out. Occasionally, one would end up on the floor and I would put it in our “I don’t have a pencil” jar so it never went to waste. My teammate did a similar thing with dry erase markers – they were regularly using them in math so it was a win-win. The kids were excited for a fresh marker and my teammate knew everyone had one for class. 

STUDENT GIFT IDEA: PRINTABLES

Another inexpensive gift option is printables. I love printing out bookmarks and giving them as student gifts. They are something that gets used immediately and are free or inexpensive. You could also make an entire activity out of it. Students can pick out a bookmark & ribbon & you can have them color it.

You can print a sheet of paper with tic-tac-toe, dots and boxes, hangman, or Wordle. If you want something more permanent, you can laminate the page so students can use a dry erase marker to play.

STUDENT GIFTS: FOOD

I know this one may be tricky because some schools don’t allow food. However, if your school is okay with outside food, I used to send home something wrapped & tell students they had to bring it home and show their parents first. A few of my favorite ideas are S’more kits, Rice Krispie treats, ice-pops, and hot chocolate. I’ve also seen people give popcorn, cookies, lollipops, and so on. 

INEXPENSIVE STUDENT GIFT: EXPERIENCES

This is another fairly inexpensive or free option. One year we asked our principal if students could bring in a stuffed animal and watch a movie in the afternoon. We’ve also done board games, decorated gingerbread houses, steam projects, crafts & activities such as mosaic art. You could really go as big or as small as you’d like. I think students just appreciate being able to take a break and hang out. If you are looking for craft ideas for your students, you can check out my youtube or a few of my other blog posts.

CLASSROOM STUDENT GIFT IDEAS: PHYSICAL ITEMS:

My biggest piece of advice regarding physical items is to always assume that whatever you give them, may stay in their desks. So fidgets, sunglasses, playdough, mystery packs and things like that may stay in their desk or bookbag and they may play with them throughout the year. You could make an announcement and give it to them at the end of the day, but there’s still a chance it’ll end up back at school so I always recommend giving things you don’t mind seeing again.

Having said all of that, a few items students seem to love and I regularly see are bubble wands, fidgets, water bottles, sunglasses, twisty straws, $2 books from Scholastic, mugs, and so on.

OTHER STUDENT GIFT IDEAS:

One of my favorite classroom gifts I received as a child was a portfolio at the end of the year. I’m in my thirties and still have all my portfolios! It was so cool to see how my work evolved but it also served as a special keepsake or memento. Examples of things in a portfolio would be writing from the year, holiday crafts, drawings, and other meaningful work. I specifically remember my kindergarten portfolio having a hand drawn family portrait and a rainbow fingerprinting.

Pictures are another great idea as well. Obviously use your discretion but over the years I’ve done career photos, holiday photos, class photos, or photos with friends. My career photos were originally part of a bulletin board that said “future doctor” or “future YouTuber” written on the child’s photo. I thought that was a fun keepsake that they can look back on when they’re older and their dreams change.
